issues.reason: The modifier of heavy_thread_day is the noun-headed 'heavy-thread', which Compound concepts never exposes ('a noun modifier is never exposed, whatever it names') and which fails the predication test — 'the day is heavy' is not what the text says — so (Inheritance heavy_thread_day heavy) asserts a property from nowhere in the sentence, and it also recurses into a modifier the decompose-once rule stops at.

The bearer is a per-binding Skolem group, so the mandated flat half would have to be a rule whose premise reads (PartOf $y (sk_vessels $x)) — a Skolem term in a premise, which 'rule premises bind through plain variables' explicitly bars, with $x free besides — so no licensed flat form exists at all and the omission is the instruction set's own leave-it-out-and-record-the-gap response, i.e. exactly the coverage gap the reviewer himself filed, not a parse defect.

gaps_confirmed: an adjective-with-PP-complement state whose bearer is a Skolem group inside a generic rule's conclusion: the dual-emit flat half is specified as a per-member (Implication (PartOf $x <group>) ...) rule and no form is given for it here
new_gaps: the gap is sharper than 'no form for nesting': with a per-binding Skolem group the per-member rule is unrepresentable in either position — nested in an asserted conclusion it is unlicensed and carries no truth value, and at top level its premise would have to contain the Skolem term (sk_vessels $x) with $x free, which the plain-variable-premise rule bars outright; a licensed carrier would need a way to distribute a property to the members of a group minted per rule-binding
defect_summary: The compliant form emits the genus (Inheritance heavy_thread_day day) and no modifier genus at all, dropping (Inheritance heavy_thread_day heavy).
